opening.greeting: Good morning, Vito. Let's process the boards.

weather.insight: Clear operating window. Good day to front-load external meetings and site movement.

opening.verse_of_the_day: This is the day that Yahweh has made. We will rejoice and be glad in it! — Psalms 118:24

anomaly.desc: JCI / IHSG spike of +1.56%; Nasdaq spike of +2.78%

market: JCI surged 1.56% to 6,186 on foreign rotation, tracking Nasdaq's 2.78% AI-driven rally.
US markets powered by Amazon's $220B capex and Nexus's $15B Anthropic data center deal.
economic: BI held rate at 5.75%, supporting rupiah stability at 18,073 amid dollar index drop.
US 10Y yield rose to 4.663%, raising capital costs for Indonesian project financing.
tech_ai: Cloud-host AI infrastructure spending is the dominant theme, benefiting data center proxies.
Nickel proxy INCO surged 5.6% on demand for data center hardware components.
political: Prabowo's KSSK meeting reinforced financial stability and market confidence commitments.
Japan's yen intervention and US rate check signal caution for regional currency volatility.

arbiter_brief: Overnight US tech surge on AI capex spills into JCI via foreign rotation, lifting the index 1.56%. Rupiah stability at 18,073 and BI's hold support sentiment, but rising US 10Y yield to 4.663% tempers venture exuberance. Commodity proxies rally on data center demand, yet high-beta plays remain vulnerable to yield-driven outflows. The VIX crash to 17 signals risk-on, but Jakarta must watch for capital cost shifts.
executive_brief: Rotate into liquid large-caps and commodity proxies to capture foreign inflow momentum.
Monitor US 10Y yield trajectory as rising rates could trigger capital outflows from Indonesia.
Leverage AI infrastructure tailwinds by positioning in data center and nickel supply chain plays.

sectors.name: Technology
sectors.ai: Indonesia's tech sector lags US peers but shows structural upside; overweight NBIS for AI-driven data center demand and ALAB for cloud migration, as US semis strength signals global capex cycle acceleration that will eventually lift ID-listed tech hardware and digital infrastructure plays.
themes: US semiconductor capex cycle, led by memory and AI chips, will drive demand for Indonesia's downstream electronics assembly and data center buildout over 12-18 months.
Indonesia's digital economy growth, with rising cloud adoption and fintech penetration, creates a durable revenue base for local tech platforms and infrastructure providers.
Government push for domestic chip manufacturing and 5G rollout provides policy tailwinds for Indonesia-focused tech hardware and telecom equipment companies.

US rate sensitivity is fading; local currency stability and BI's dovish stance support margin expansion for ID-focused financials, reducing exposure to global volatility.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
sectors.ai: Indonesia's renewables sector shows strong momentum, with PLUG and NRG leading gains. Watch for policy catalysts from the upcoming national energy plan revision and potential tariff adjustments for solar and battery storage. Focus on local manufacturing plays tied to nickel downstreaming and geothermal expansion, as these offer direct exposure to Indonesia's structural energy transition without relying on volatile global clean-tech sentiment.
themes: Indonesia's nickel downstreaming policy creates a durable competitive advantage for domestic battery and energy storage supply chains, insulating local players from global price swings.
Geothermal development remains a structural growth driver, supported by government targets to increase capacity by 3.5 GW by 2030 and favorable feed-in tariffs.
The revision of the National Energy Plan (RUEN) is expected to mandate higher renewable energy mix targets, directly benefiting solar and wind project developers and local equipment manufacturers.

sectors.name: Healthcare
sectors.ai: Indonesia's healthcare sector shows relative strength (+0.72%) versus US weakness, signaling domestic resilience. Key movers like SRAJ and MICE indicate local demand momentum. Capitalize on this divergence by overweighting Indonesian hospital and pharma names, as structural underpenetration and rising medical tourism drive durable growth.
themes: Rising middle-class healthcare spending in Indonesia, with private insurance penetration growing at 8% CAGR, underpins sustained demand for hospital and diagnostic services.
Government push for domestic pharmaceutical self-sufficiency, via mandatory local sourcing and tax incentives, creates long-term tailwinds for Indonesian drug manufacturers like SRAJ.
Medical tourism expansion, targeting 5 million foreign patients by 2025, boosts premium hospital chains and specialized care providers in Jakarta and Bali.

core.label: Real GDP Growth
core.commentary: Annual growth is firm, but the quarter contracted and government consumption was a major driver.

core.label: PMI-BI Manufacturing
core.commentary: Manufacturing remains above the 50 expansion threshold; the next-quarter expectation is stronger.

core.label: Consumer Confidence
core.commentary: Consumers remain optimistic, but the level alone does not establish improvement from May.

core.label: Retail Sales Index
core.commentary: The expected index remains high, but the monthly contraction points to softer near-term spending.

core.label: Headline CPI Inflation
core.commentary: Headline inflation accelerated and is close to the upper edge of Bank Indonesia's target corridor.

core.label: Core Inflation
core.commentary: Core inflation rose but remains inside the policy target corridor, indicating contained underlying pressure.

core.label: Volatile Food Inflation
core.commentary: Food inflation eased from May, although its level remains high enough to pressure household purchasing power.

core.label: Administered-Price Inflation
core.commentary: Regulated-price inflation accelerated sharply as non-subsidised fuel and airfares increased.

core.label: BI Policy Rate
core.commentary: The higher policy setting supports rupiah stability while raising domestic funding and valuation hurdles.

core.label: FX Reserves
core.commentary: Reserve cover remains adequate; the key watch is whether rupiah defence causes persistent drawdowns.

core.label: Trade Balance
core.commentary: The monthly deficit weakens near-term FX support even though the year-to-date balance remains positive.

core.label: Current Account
core.commentary: The deficit is manageable but increases dependence on direct and portfolio investment inflows.

core.label: APBN Deficit
core.commentary: The first-half deficit is contained, while the full-year outlook is close enough to the legal ceiling to monitor.

core.label: Credit Growth / Gross NPL
core.commentary: Lending is expanding while headline asset quality remains contained.

detail.label: Business Activity Survey
detail.commentary: The higher weighted net balance indicates broader business expansion.

detail.label: Wholesale Price Inflation
detail.commentary: Upstream price pressure is elevated and may pass through to producer margins and consumer prices.

detail.label: External Debt
detail.commentary: Currency mix and near-term refinancing needs matter more than the headline stock.

detail.label: Revenue / Spending
detail.commentary: Revenue quality and productive spending composition determine the growth impact.

detail.label: Unemployment / Average Wage
detail.commentary: Unemployment improved, while real wage growth and formal-job quality remain the key checks.

detail.label: Net NPL / Loan at Risk
detail.commentary: Both arrears and broader restructured exposures should stay contained as credit expands.

detail.label: CAR / LCR
